title: Opaque session propagation and non-intrusive stream-tap adapters across SDKs
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce opaque session propagation token to preserve session affinity across stream reconnects; add non-intrusive StreamTap adapter for telemetry and debugging without changing backpressure semantics; SDK surface parity and minor version bumps.
description: Context: Customers reported resumed streaming sessions lost context on reconnect and telemetry hooks were invasive for production use. This PR introduces an opaque session token propagation mechanism across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs and a StreamTap adapter that lets observability and local debugging tools inspect stream events without altering timing or backpressure. Motivation: Provide a small, low-risk surface that solves two operational problems: 1) make reconnect/resume deterministic for applications using session affinity and 2) enable safe passive telemetry for streaming workloads. Summary of changes: Added opaque session header (X-Redwood-Session) and a lightweight session encoder/decoder; implemented session-preserve logic in the streaming reconnect shim; added StreamTap adapter (pluggable middleware) that exposes a read-only stream of events for observers; harmonized retry presets so resume attempts are marked idempotent to avoid double-exec semantics; bump SDK versions: python->1.9.0, typescript->2.4.3, go->v1.6.1; included unit and e2e streaming tests and an integration test that simulates reconnect sequences and in-flight KV cache reuse. Checklist: - add session header and helpers across SDKs; - add StreamTap adapter and examples; - ensure backpressure invariants hold under adapter; - update SDK docs and changelogs; - add e2e harness and flaky test allowances. Changed areas: ["sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py","sdk/typescript/src/stream/streamTap.ts","sdk/go/stream/adapter/tap.go","sdk/common/session/session.go","docs/sdk/streaming.md","tests/e2e/stream_reconnect_sim.py","examples/stream-tap/README.md","changelogs/python.md","changelogs/typescript.md","changelogs/go.md","ci/e2e-stream-harness.yml"]. Patch snippets (illustrative): ["// streamTap: observe events without modifying data or timing; read-only interface","const tap = new StreamTap(observer => { observer.on('chunk', c => log(c)); });","// server-side: accept X-Redwood-Session header and route to affinity pool","sessionToken := req.Header.Get(\"X-Redwood-Session\") // opaque string"]. Review thread summary: "Initial review requested smaller surface for Go impl. Diego called out potential race on session cache invalidation and asked for a stronger test that simulates concurrent reconnects; addressed by adding a mutex around cache promotion and a dedicated concurrent_reconnect test; Samir requested ergonomics tweaks for TypeScript (StreamTap factory signature) which were applied; Lena verified python tests and asked for doc examples demonstrating telemetry use-cases; author responded with examples and a short video capture for reviewers. One CI flake on integration tests caused a rerun; fixed a timing race in the e2e harness and re-ran. Merge: squash merge after final signoff. Merge method: squash. Motivation/risks: The changes are additive and guarded behind a feature flag in the SDKs (enabled by default for 1.9.0/2.4.3/v1.6.1). Risk surface: small risk for customers that proxy headers are stripped by intermediate infra; added robust fallback to a generated ephemeral session. Rollout plan: gradually enable GA by flipping the feature flag for Hosted API customers in the next 2 weeks; monitor metrics (session-resume-rate, duplicate-event-rate, latency p95) via new dashboards. Post-merge tasks: create a compatibility note for on-prem/private installers (redwood-private-installer), land a small patch to server routing to accept the opaque token in legacy gateways, coordinate marketing changelog entry, and file a follow-up to add optional HMAC signing (ENG-21110). Related items: ENG-20934 (session affinity work), PM-4101 (obs requirements), SUP-782 (customer incident).
